node-1.label: Slightly pruritic lesions on the face for 1 year

node-2.label: Patient is a girl younger than 2 years, born after an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, with growth and development appropriate for age

node-3.label: No associated symptoms such as fever, anorexia, or weight loss were noted

node-4.label: Physical examination revealed multiple skin-colored and erythematous follicular papules (1-2 mm) in a segmental pattern on the right forehead, dorsum and tip of nose; a small excoriated plaque on the right malar area; no mucosal lesions; rest of examination unremarkable

why.why: Histopathology showing follicular mucinosis with mucin deposition and no cytological atypia favors an inflammatory dermatosis rather than a benign nevoid/segmental lesion; the Radiologist explicitly favors follicular mucinosis over a nevoid lesion. The segmental pattern and young age are still compatible with a benign local process, so a small possibility remains, but confidence is reduced from 0.45 to 0.2.

Histopathology demonstrates follicular and sebaceous epithelial mucin deposition with Alcian blue positivity, mild lymphocytic infiltrate, and no atypia or epidermotropism, which is characteristic of follicular mucinosis, a chronic inflammatory dermatosis. The clinical segmental pruritic pattern and absence of systemic symptoms fit this entity, and both the Pathologist and Radiologist analyses support it. Confidence is increased from 0.4 to 0.9.

Histopathology shows mucin deposition and only a mild lymphocytic infiltrate without features of infection, and the chronic localized course without systemic symptoms makes infection unlikely. Expert analyses explicitly refute infection, so confidence is reduced from 0.1 to 0.02.

Histopathology reveals a benign inflammatory pattern without systemic involvement, and the patient has normal growth, development, and no systemic symptoms. Both expert analyses confirm benignity and refute systemic/metabolic disease, so confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.01.

node-9.label: Skin biopsy histopathology shows follicular and sebaceous epithelial mucin deposition with Alcian blue positivity, mild lymphocytic infiltrate, and no cytological atypia or epidermotropism

node-10.label: The facial lesion is follicular mucinosis

why.why: The Pathologist analysis explicitly confirms that the biopsy findings (follicular and sebaceous epithelial mucin deposition, Alcian blue positivity, mild lymphocytic infiltrate, no atypia or epidermotropism) are consistent with follicular mucinosis and that current evidence sufficiently supports a benign reactive process. This strengthens the specific diagnosis of follicular mucinosis in this young child with segmental pruritic facial papules. Confidence is raised slightly from 0.85 to 0.88, but remains below absolute because T-cell receptor gene rearrangement results are still pending and early mycosis fungoides cannot be completely excluded.

node-11.label: T-cell receptor gene rearrangement results are pending/not yet available

node-12.label: Early mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) presenting as follicular mucinosis

attrs.why: Follicular mucinosis is a known histologic pattern that can be associated with early mycosis fungoides, and the T-cell receptor gene rearrangement results are still pending, so a clonal T-cell population has not been excluded. However, the biopsy shows no cytological atypia or epidermotropism, the patient is a young child with a chronic localized course, and the Pathologist analysis favors a benign reactive process, so confidence in early mycosis fungoides is low at 0.15.
